evidence: Kew/POWO accepts Panicum virgatum and lists Texas in its native range.
Hagenbuch & Lemke's Texas Hill Country grass appendix explicitly records Hays County (Bierner 90-208, TEX-LL).
The same appendix explicitly records Blanco County (Breckenridge 559, SWT).
The same appendix explicitly records Val Verde County (Smith & Butterwick 202, TEX-LL).
target_zone_range.guardrail: Occurrence is not treated as nativity; introduced records do not count toward the three-county native threshold.

morphology.look_here_first: Look at the base/collar and then the seedhead: a tall warm-season rhizomatous clump with a broad airy pyramidal panicle and a conspicuously hairy ligule/collar zone.
diagnostic_traits: ligule a ciliolate membrane with conspicuous collar hairs

confusers.separator: Kleingrass can resemble switchgrass in the panicle, but is an introduced African bunchgrass with a firm knotty base; switchgrass is native and rhizomatous.
Hall's panicum is much shorter, glaucous, mostly basal-leaved, and has a smaller stiffer panicle.

installation_guardrail: Do not install until Calvin explicitly approves B009 pass taxa.
